mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to edge up while TRANSIT remains less negative, then more commuters will pass through commercial corridors and convert weekday trips into retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both becoming less negative for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in RESIDENTIAL time signals more time spent outside the home; within one to two weeks that shift should translate into higher discretionary retail visits and a smaller negative RETAIL_REC reading.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1.0 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or becomes more negative over the next 14 days after a week-on-week drop in RESIDENTIAL of at least 1.0 point.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS rebounds while GROCERY_PHARM also improves, it indicates broader out-of-home activity and errands; that mix should spill over into retail-and-recreation demand within four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains more negative over the next 28 days even though PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both trend upward for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls further below its current level and WORKPLACES do not recover, then commuting and downtown traffic will weaken, suppressing retail footfall and pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT declines by 2.0 points or more week-on-week while WORKPLACES does not improve
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises relative to the last 28 days even after a transit drop of at least 2.0 points with no concurrent WORKPLACES improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week improvement in PARKS during late spring reflects warmer-weather outdoor substitution that draws discretionary trips away from indoor retail, so RETAIL_REC should soften over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5.0 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not become more negative within 7 to 14 days after a PARKS increase of at least 5.0 points.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both stay elevated, households consolidate trips near home and reduce discretionary shopping elsewhere, which should hold RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain elevated relative to the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES crosses above its recent level of stagnation and TRANSIT also turns less negative, that synchronized mobility recovery should increase downtown shopping trips and raise RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above its prior two-week mean and TRANSIT improves in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after WORKPLACES rises above its prior two-week mean and TRANSIT also improves.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM combined with a continued drop in RESIDENTIAL indicates more out-of-home errands and less at-home time; that pattern should mildly lift retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not become less negative over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising and RESIDENTIAL keeps falling.
